events.title: Munich Agreement Signed
events.description: Britain, France, Italy, and Germany signed the Munich Agreement, permitting Nazi Germany to annex the Sudetenland region of Czechoslovakia. Czechoslovakia was not invited to the negotiations. British Prime Minister Neville Chamberlain returned home declaring he had secured 'peace for our time.'
events.significance: The agreement became the emblematic example of the failed policy of appeasement. Germany occupied the rest of Czechoslovakia in March 1939, and World War II began less than a year later.

events.title: Nuremberg Trials Verdicts Delivered
events.description: The International Military Tribunal at Nuremberg delivered its verdicts against 22 major Nazi leaders on September 30 and October 1, 1946. The judgments were read out over two days, with twelve defendants sentenced to death and others receiving prison terms or acquittals.
events.significance: The trials established key principles of international criminal law, including individual accountability for war crimes, crimes against humanity, and crimes against peace, and shaped later international tribunals.

events.title: Berlin Airlift Ends
events.description: The Berlin Airlift officially ended after Western Allied aircraft delivered more than 2.3 million tons of food, fuel, and supplies to West Berlin. The operation had begun in June 1948 in response to the Soviet blockade of the city's western sectors, though the blockade itself was lifted in May 1949.
events.significance: The airlift demonstrated Western resolve and logistical capability early in the Cold War, strengthened ties among the Allies, and helped lead to the formation of NATO.

events.title: 30 September Movement in Indonesia
events.description: In the early hours of October 1 (beginning the night of September 30), a group calling itself the 30 September Movement abducted and killed six senior army generals in Jakarta. General Suharto quickly took control of the army and crushed the movement.
events.significance: The events led to the mass anti-communist killings of 1965-66, the destruction of the Indonesian Communist Party, the decline of President Sukarno, and the rise of Suharto's 30-year New Order regime.

events.title: Birth of the Modern Hormone Therapy Pioneer Era Marker: Babe Ruth Hits 60th Home Run
events.description: Babe Ruth of the New York Yankees hit his 60th home run of the 1927 season against the Washington Senators at Yankee Stadium, setting a single-season record.
events.significance: The record stood until 1961 and made the 1927 Yankees one of the most celebrated teams in baseball history, cementing Ruth's legendary status.
